overview: This four-page file concerns the application of Japanese communications law in colonial Taiwan. Its principal document is a June 7, 1937 despatch from American Vice Consul Alvin T. Rowe, Jr., at Taihoku, explaining that Imperial Japanese postal, telegraph, wireless, telephone, railway-mail, and shipping-mail laws applied in Taiwan and that the few local regulations differed chiefly in administrative terminology and procedure. Two later State Department communications transmitted copies of the despatch to the Department of Commerce and the Federal Communications Commission.

subfiles.title: Despatch on communications laws applicable in Taiwan
subfiles.from: Alvin T. Rowe, Jr., American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports on whether Taiwan had special local communications laws distinct from those of Japan proper.
subfiles.summary: Rowe responds to an April 19, 1937 State Department instruction asking him to verify an earlier statement that Japanese communications laws and regulations applied in Taiwan without materially distinct local rules. Citing the Chief of the Superintendent's Division in the Bureau of Communications and Transport of the Taiwan Government General, he explains that two Imperial ordinances extended Japanese laws to Taiwan and that Taiwan Government General Ordinance No. 80 governed their local enforcement. Any minor local provisions reportedly reproduced Japanese rules except for administrative names, official titles, and small procedural details; after consulting the Consulate General in Tokyo, the consulate concluded that separate translations of such local decrees were unnecessary.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Taihoku despatch to the Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of the June 7 despatch concerning Taiwan's communications laws.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State forwards to the Secretary of Commerce a copy of American Vice Consul Rowe's Despatch No. 17 from Taihoku, dated June 7, 1937. The brief communication identifies the enclosure as concerning the communications laws of Taiwan.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Taihoku despatch to the Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: The Acting Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.about: Transmits the June 7 Taihoku despatch to the Law Department of the Federal Communications Commission.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State sends the Acting Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission a copy of Despatch No. 17 from the American Vice Consul at Taihoku. Intended for the Commission's Law Department, the enclosure concerns the communications laws applicable in Taiwan.

interest: The file succinctly documents how Japan incorporated colonial Taiwan into its metropolitan communications-law regime while retaining minor local administrative adaptations. It is useful for studying legal integration within the Japanese Empire, the Taiwan Government General's regulatory role, and American efforts to map foreign communications systems during the interwar period. The two transmittals also show that the findings circulated beyond the State Department to agencies concerned with commerce and communications regulation.
